newsitem.title: CANADA: CP Rail says Vancouver unloading delayed.
newsitem.headline: CP Rail says Vancouver unloading delayed.

text.p: A bottleneck of 3,000 CP Rail System hopper cars at Vancouver delayed CP's movement of grains and oilseeds by three days since mid-April, a CP statement said Thursday.
"The continuing delays at Vancouver are clogging the entire grain transportation system," said Rick Sallee, vice-president of CP's agri coal group.

Grain shipment delays led to a backlog of vessels on Canada's West Coast from January to March, costing the Canadian Wheat Board more than C$15 million in demurrage with one ship waiting as long as 62 days to load.
"We're now seeing the impact of slow unloads with average cycle times for grain trains from the Prairies increasing by three days during the last four weeks," Sallee said.
A daily average of 217 railcars were unloaded, 36 percent of the daily average of 596 railcars available in Vancouver.

"The problem at the Port of Vancouver appears to be two-fold: too few vessels in loading position and, despite sufficient port inventories and a seven-day-a-week work schedule at the port, an inadequate supply of the required grains to fill the vessels that are ready to load," Sallee said.
